Problem column: "Stage F number literals: jsonschema/v6 v6.0.3 reads instance numbers with big.Rat.SetString (isInteger, numValidate, equals, writeHash); its time grows with the square of the mantissa and with 10^|exponent|, and it returns nil above |exponent| 10^6, which numValidate and writeHash dereference. Decision column: "WP-35's number model (schemaview numbers.go) hands the validator each KindInt/KindFloat literal as written when it lies on the view's grid (multiples of 10^-F below 10^I in magnitude, I and F at least 40 and covering every view number) in at most 64 bytes; in normalized form when longer; otherwise as a bounded surrogate with the literal's integrality, order against every view number, multipleOf divisibility and, in a view with uniqueItems, exact equality with other instance numbers. No literal is refused, and stage F's diagnostics are those of the literal. A jsonschema/v6 panic is RZ-CFG-005 'cannot be validated: the schema validator failed' at the root. A number node whose text is outside RFC 8259 (excluded by the tree contract) skips the validator with RZ-CFG-005 'cannot be validated: a number is not an RFC 8259 number literal' at its position. Compile refuses a view whose numbers need more than 400 integer or fraction digits, or whose multipleOf period exceeds 400 digits (ErrSchema), before compiling it."

deviations: Of the three approaches the finding offered, I chose (a), the surrogate with no new refusal. For multipleOf, the surrogate keeps residues modulo the period Q (exactly for small shifts; for large shifts, 0 modulo the 2 and 5 part and the mantissa modulo the coprime part). The finding's sketch mentioned only a clamped magnitude and a truncated fraction, which do not preserve divisibility for multipleOf values with factors other than 2 and 5. The one refusal added is Compile's, of views (which only Ruralz authors) whose numbers need more than 400 digits; it is filed in contractRequests. No configuration input is refused, so the owner decision on a config-side limit that the finding mentions is not needed. I still filed the R row so the bound is recorded.

A view without uniqueItems, which includes the rendered view, tags every off-grid value 0. Two distinct off-grid values can then share a surrogate. That is sound because uniqueItems is the only jsonschema/v6 path that compares two instance numbers. The tags' map lookup hashes the full exact-value key, so in a view with uniqueItems it is a span that cannot yield; the Options doc says so. The rendered view does not use uniqueItems, so production never builds tags.

Bounded retained heap is asserted with a deterministic counter: the summed bit lengths of the big.Rat values held in the validation error kinds, at most 512 bits per number. A sampled heap measurement is not used, following AGENTS.md's rule on deterministic tests.
